announcements.name: Windows 11 developer configuration image in public preview
announcements.shortDescription: A developer-optimized marketplace image that arrives pre-loaded with Visual Studio, Git, GitHub CLI, Python, Node.js, GitHub Copilot, and WSL with Ubuntu already configured.
announcements.longDescription: Windows 365 now supports a new Windows 11 developer configuration image in public preview, delivering a developer-optimized Cloud PC that is ready to go on sign-in rather than a vanilla machine. Tools like Visual Studio, Git, GitHub CLI, Python, Node.js, and GitHub Copilot are already installed, and WSL with Ubuntu is set up so developers can work across both Windows and Linux workflows. It also includes developer-focused settings and Windows configurations to cut down setup friction and get to a first commit faster. The environment can be further customized with the exact SDKs, CLIs, packages, and build tools a project requires while staying within enterprise guardrails.

announcements.name: Windows 365 for Agents is generally available
announcements.shortDescription: Gives AI agents their own Cloud PCs with full Windows environments so they can see, interact with apps, and operate as a person would.
announcements.longDescription: Windows 365 for Agents is generally available, giving AI agents their own Cloud PC with a full Windows environment so they can see, interact with apps, and operate the way a person would. It addresses three problems agent builders face: the GUI gap (work that happens in graphical line-of-business apps and browser portals built for humans, not APIs), the legacy gap (mainframe terminal emulators and desktop-only tools that can be automated as-is without API wrapping or screen-scraping), and the scale gap (managing images, security, and lifecycle when going from one agent to many). The platform provides pooled Cloud PCs managed at scale and governed by IT, the same way an organization manages a fleet of employee machines.

announcements.name: New 32-core SKU with up to 128 GB RAM
announcements.shortDescription: Expands the diversity of Cloud PC compute options for memory-intensive local AI workloads.
announcements.longDescription: Windows 365 offers a diversity of Cloud PC SKUs, including a new 32-core SKU supporting up to 128 GB RAM [inferred] (stated in the transcript as "128-gigabit RAM"). This expanded compute is aimed at running AI models directly on the developer-controlled Cloud PC environment, where available RAM and CPU can be used flexibly without incurring additional token-based costs. In the demo, the presenter uses VS Code and Microsoft Foundry's model catalog to filter and run a small Qwen model locally on CPU, noting that the number of models that can run is limited only by available free RAM.

announcements.name: MCP tool layer for agents
announcements.shortDescription: A set of Model Context Protocol tools lets any MCP-speaking agent framework provision, connect to, interact with, and manage the lifecycle of a Cloud PC, managed through the Agent 365 portal.
announcements.longDescription: Windows 365 for Agents includes an MCP tool layer built on the Model Context Protocol, the open standard for connecting agents to tools. Microsoft ships a set of MCP tools that let an agent provision a Cloud PC, connect to it, interact with it, and manage its lifecycle, so any agent framework that speaks MCP works with Windows 365 for Agents. The MCP tools are managed through the Agent 365 portal, with observability and governance surfacing the same way as for any Agent 365-enabled agent, while Cloud PC pools are managed in Intune and identity goes through Entra ID. Integration is demonstrated using the A365 toolkit and a tooling manifest that declares which MCP servers the agent can access.
